project_context: Boundary-Aware Claim Evaluation of historical ESRS-style disclosures generated by a fixed evidence-card RAG workflow

standard_basis.version_policy: Use the same 2023 requirement definitions as the existing E1 tasks. Do not interpret these identifiers using the renumbered 2026 revision.

design_notes.purpose: Research proposal for four tasks per standard; not a frozen or activated runtime configuration.
selection_principles: A mix of narrative and quantitative content
No selection based on BACE-comparator score differences
design_notes.historical_interpretation: 2019-2023 cases are ESRS-style simulations, not claims that these reports were legally subject to ESRS.
design_notes.missing_evidence_policy: Distinguish explicit absence, explicit zero, non-disclosure, unavailable source, and retrieval failure. Missing evidence does not establish that a policy, target, incident or action does not exist.
design_notes.source_quality_policy: CSV metrics are eligible only after their meaning, population, period, unit and source passage have been checked. Existing extracted cells are discovery aids, not ground truth.
design_notes.temporal_policy: Freeze document eligibility and publication cutoff before retrieval. Do not import later policies or targets into earlier cases. Preserve observation year and source-publication year separately.
design_notes.generation_policy: Use the same shared generation instructions across E1, S1 and G1. Task risk notes are researcher metadata, not evaluator-specific hints for the generator.
design_notes.implementation_note: These files follow the existing task-spec field structure. Extra research metadata does not implement source checks, missingness handling or runtime integration.

tasks.task_name: Business conduct policies and corporate culture
tasks.task_scope: Business-conduct policies, corporate culture, code of conduct, reporting channels, whistleblower protection, policy scope, and responsible functions.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests governance commitments and policy boundaries. Detailed anti-corruption procedures and training performance are reserved for G1-3.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 7-11. Business conduct policies and corporate culture.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: Historical codes of conduct and governance or compliance report sections are candidate sources. A hotline does not by itself establish anonymity, non-retaliation or independent investigation.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company- and reporting-year-specific source passages and tables about business-conduct policies, corporate culture, code of conduct, reporting channels, whistleblower protection, policy scope, and responsible functions.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure section about business conduct policies and corporate culture using only evidence supplied for the case, preserving its factual qualifications.
claim_risk_notes: Do not infer an effective ethical culture from the existence of a code.
Distinguish confidential reporting, anonymity and protection against retaliation.
Do not infer independent investigation from an externally operated hotline.
Do not claim universal employee or supplier coverage without evidence.
Do not substitute board diversity or remuneration under ESRS 2 GOV for G1 business conduct.

tasks.task_scope: Supplier relationship management, procurement risks, social and environmental selection criteria, supplier assessment and development, and policies to prevent late payment, especially to SMEs.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Adds substantive supply-chain management coverage and prevents the four-task governance set from consisting entirely of internal compliance disclosures.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 12-15; application requirements AR 2-3. Management of relationships with suppliers.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: BASF and Evonik 2023 reports contain supplier selection, assessment, training and development evidence. The core is management practice; full payment-performance measurement belongs to G1-6.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company- and reporting-year-specific source passages and tables about supplier relationship management, procurement risks, social and environmental selection criteria, supplier assessment and development, and policies to prevent late payment, especially to SMEs.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure section about management of relationships with suppliers using only evidence supplied for the case, preserving its factual qualifications.
claim_risk_notes: An audit or assessment does not establish that every supplier complies.
Preserve direct versus indirect supplier and spend-versus-supplier-count denominators.
Do not attribute all industry-initiative audits to the company.
Supplier-worker impacts belong to S2 unless used specifically as evidence of procurement management.
A payment policy or a threshold such as paid within 60 days is not an observed average payment time.

tasks.task_name: Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery
tasks.task_scope: Procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery; investigator independence, reporting to governing bodies, policy communication and anti-corruption training.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests whether operational control and training claims are supported, while keeping allegations and incident outcomes in G1-4.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 16-21; application requirements AR 4-8. Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue contains 21 training-related indicator definitions and nonempty extracted cells in all 25 development company-years. General compliance training must be distinguished from anti-corruption training.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company- and reporting-year-specific source passages and tables about procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery; investigator independence, reporting to governing bodies, policy communication and anti-corruption training.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure section about prevention and detection of corruption and bribery using only evidence supplied for the case, preserving its factual qualifications.
claim_risk_notes: Do not label all compliance training as anti-corruption training.
Do not confuse participants, unique people, completions, hours and coverage percentages.
Retain the correct denominator for functions at risk.
Do not infer control effectiveness or absence of corruption from training coverage.
Do not infer independence from an investigator's job title or external hotline operation.

tasks.task_scope: Reporting-period corruption and bribery convictions, fines and actions addressing breaches; confirmed incidents, disciplinary measures, business-partner consequences and legal-case outcomes when disclosed.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Provides an incident-and-outcome task with substantively distinct allegation, confirmation and legal-status boundaries. Retention is conditional on a source audit because historical coverage is uneven.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 22-26. Incidents of corruption or bribery.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue has five indicator definitions and nonempty extracted cells in only 10 of 25 development company-years. Evonik 2023 demonstrates that extracted values can mislabel alleged cases and general compliance outcomes as confirmed corruption.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company- and reporting-year-specific source passages and tables about reporting-period corruption and bribery convictions, fines and actions addressing breaches; confirmed incidents, disciplinary measures, business-partner consequences and legal-case outcomes when disclosed.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure section about incidents of corruption or bribery using only evidence supplied for the case, preserving its factual qualifications.
claim_risk_notes: Allegations, investigations, confirmed incidents and convictions are different statuses.
Do not treat all compliance dismissals or terminated contracts as corruption outcomes.
No convictions or no material cases does not establish no incidents.
Retain currency, reporting period, recognition basis and company involvement.
Do not treat missing evidence as zero, or a policy statement as an incident outcome.
A heading mentioning confirmed incidents cannot override qualifying text describing allegations.
